items.title: Personalized gene therapy relieves severe epilepsy in two boys
items.summary: Switching off one copy of a gene also enabled one of the children to walk independently for the first time.

items.title: Inside the high-stakes race to develop an Ebola vaccine for an escalating outbreak
items.summary: The University of Oxford has already vaccinated its first clinical-trial participant. The study’s lead scientist Teresa Lambe tells Nature how they were able to move so fast.

items.title: Bizarre CRISPR enzyme kills cancer cells by shredding their DNA
items.summary: Early tests suggest the protein can be aimed at targets with tumour-causing mutations.

items.title: This El Niño is set to be the largest on record by a ‘mind-blowing margin’
items.summary: Forecasters predict that the monster climate pattern will combine with global warming to push global temperatures in 2027 to new heights.

items.title: It’ll grow on you: live fungi formed into sustainable fashion
items.summary: Textile made from fungal filaments can repair itself and is biodegradable.

items.title: Skin cancer spreads between catfish in a freshwater lake
items.summary: The discovery of a transmissible melanoma in a freshwater catfish raises questions about the disease’s origin, mode of transmission and broader impact on the species.

items.title: When should you treat a fever? Evolution holds the answer
items.summary: Understanding natural selection can improve medical treatments, social policies and crop yields.

items.title: Breathalyser can tell if you are burning fat from a single exhalation
items.summary: The compact device can measure when the body is in ketosis and could help people to manage weight loss.

items.title: What counts as a moon? Huge ‘exosatellite’ sparks debate
items.summary: Discovery of a distant Jupiter-mass object could pave the way for detection of exomoons — plus, a rare transmissible cancer found in catfish.

items.title: CRISPR–Cas regulates expression of embedded anti-phage defence systems
items.summary: CRISPR–Cas systems transcriptionally tune diverse innate defences using CRISPR RNA-like guides to balance antiviral protection with fitness, and hyperactivate these defences when compromised, establishing a layered bacterial ‘immunity guard’ network.

items.title: Prior therapy defines mutation profiles in childhood cancer at relapse
items.summary: Chemotherapy, particularly with platinum-based drugs, is associated with substantial, rapidly detectable mutagenesis in childhood cancers, tripling private signatures and doubling mutation burden, highlighting therapy-induced tumour evolution and opportunities for safer, de-escalated treatment.

items.title: Wildfires rampaged across Europe in the dying days of the Triassic

items.title: All living things emit a faint glow. Could this light be useful?
items.summary: Ultra-weak ‘biophotons’ might be used to diagnose disease, or could even represent a new signalling mechanism in cells.

items.title: Humanity spoke thousands of languages at the dawn of farming — now many of them are lost

items.title: Structures and inhibition of the Crimean–Congo haemorrhagic fever virus polymerase
items.summary: Structural studies of Crimean–Congo haemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) polymerase reveal the structural basis of CCHFV RNA synthesis and highlight druggable sites for designing both nucleoside antivirals and non-nucleoside antivirals.

items.title: Non-epitaxial perovskite polariton laser diode operating under direct current
items.summary: By integrating a solution-grown perovskite microplate with chemically inert single-walled carbon nanotube electrodes and embedding them into an optical microcavity, the new microdevices can achieve polariton lasing under a constant direct current at 8 K.
